style.prompt: A bright, friendly educational animation of the water cycle over a sunny blue ocean, widescreen. Seconds 0-3: the sun warms the ocean and wisps of water vapor rise upward from the water surface; the single on-screen label "Evaporation" appears in clean white bold letters. Seconds 3-6: high in the sky the rising vapor gathers and cools into fluffy white clouds that grow larger and darker; the label changes to "Condensation". Seconds 6-10: the clouds release rain that falls back down into the ocean; the label changes to "Precipitation". Only one label is on screen at a time, spelled exactly Evaporation, then Condensation, then Precipitation. No other text, no captions, no subtitles, no logos, no watermarks. Audio: a warm, friendly narrator voice-over says: "The sun warms the ocean, and water rises into the air. That is evaporation. Up high, the vapor cools and forms clouds. That is condensation. When the clouds get heavy, water falls as rain. That is precipitation!" Soft, gentle background music.
